A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same audio-probing study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched reliably across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original frozen-backbone probing experiments on general audio, bioacoustic and single-label tasks, including mAP and accuracy results with seed variability in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments and adds baseline results and original prototype-count and binarization ablations in Appendix B, Table 7.

M1.justification: Protobin retains STE-trained binary prototypes, cosine matching, spatial max pooling and an unrestricted linear classifier. v3 explicitly describes the existing class-agnostic design and absence of an orthogonality loss. Protofloat is introduced as an ablation control, rather than a revision of the proposed protobin procedure.

E1.justification: The actual coverage remains five general multi-label datasets, seven BirdSet subsets and two single-label tasks, as confirmed by v1 Table 7 and v3 Table 8. The new ablations reuse as20k, urban and esc50 without introducing different task requirements or input conditions.

E2.justification: v3 adds the frequency-concatenation and temporal-pooling baseline linpre, attributed to Niizumi et al. (2022), to Table 2's general-audio comparisons. Appendix B also introduces protofloat as a comparator for separating binarization from architectural simplification. Existing benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported prototype count from 20 per class on every dataset to 10 for as20k and 20 elsewhere. Appendix B introduces controlled sweeps over 1, 5, 10 and 20 prototypes per class. Other benchmark settings remain stable. v3 Table 10 still lists 20 universally, so the PDFs do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new Appendix B systematically tests prototype-count sensitivity across five backbones and three tasks. It also compares proto, protobin and a class-agnostic protofloat control to distinguish binarization effects from the combined architectural simplifications. v1 contains no equivalent controlled analyses of these central design choices.

E5.justification: The retained benchmark continues reporting five-seed means and standard deviations, with the same one-standard-deviation criterion for pairwise wins. The new ablation reports means across three seeds without dispersion estimates. This introduces a different reporting practice for the added study, without documenting fewer runs for existing results or a new significance test.

E6.justification: v3 adds linpre scores and substantial prototype-count and precision comparisons in Table 7. For example, the new study reports EAT/urban protobin rising from 80.05 to 89.24 mAP as prototypes per class increase from 1 to 20. Existing Appendix Tables 4–6 retain their values. Main Table 3 changes ASiT/esc50 protobin from 79.3 to 80.3 accuracy, while Table 6 still reports 79.25, preventing interpretation as a verified same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The symbolic parameter-count calculation for EP changes from DC + 2D in v1 Table 8 to D² + QD + DC in v3 Table 9. This is a limited mathematical correction. The central pooling derivation and computational run-count equations are retained; the expanded near-orthogonality discussion supplies heuristic reasoning rather than a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion narrow the broad claim that audio SSL defaults to fine-tuning to the pursuit of state-of-the-art performance on AudioSet. The central pooling-bottleneck and prototypical-probing claims remain. The contribution list now explicitly highlights class-agnostic prototypes and elimination of an explicit orthogonality loss.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the proposed explanation for emergent prototype near-orthogonality. Appendix B newly attributes performance gains primarily to architectural simplification and interprets binarization as a precision–memory tradeoff. It also discusses prototype-count saturation and task-dependent situations favoring float or class-dependent prototypes. These are substantive additions to the mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces a generic GitHub homepage with a specific anonymous repository link. v3 more explicitly documents linpre and the prototype variants, revises EP's reported parameter count from approximately 9.2k to 622k, and identifies Table 3's fine-tuning scores as originating in the backbone papers. Hardware, caching, BirdSet augmentation and search-range disclosures remain stable.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises its positioning by acknowledging established audio-probing work and HEAR evaluations, adding discussion and citations including Niizumi, Turian, Li, Yadav and Pepino. It focuses the research gap more specifically on pooling and AudioSet evaluation, incorporates the earlier token-reshaping approach, and explains its relationship to prior class-dependent prototypical methods more fully.

P1.justification: Substantial framing and explanatory rewrites span the introduction, contribution list, related work, method rationale and several results discussions. The contributions are reordered, and the new ablation appendix is integrated before the retained resource and implementation appendices. These changes materially reshape the narrative beyond local copyediting.

P2.justification: v3 adds the ablation table, expands Table 2 and the pooling-method overview with linpre columns, and adds publication-year annotations to Figure 6. Captions and placements receive limited adjustments. Most figures and the overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: The added pooling baseline and targeted ablations make the method's advantages and design choices easier to assess. More precise research positioning and a concrete code-access link also improve the paper. These gains are limited by mean-only ablation reporting, claims of consistent/significant advantages that overstate the mixed Table 7 results, and unresolved prototype-count and ASiT/esc50 inconsistencies between the main text and appendices.
